brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut to bring our cap price down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc, backed by the market ask (₹0.55–1.20/pc) and four strong alternates ready to qualify.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging, targeting the lower end of the market band.
priceAsk.target: Target price of ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps, versus the market asking range of ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc)
priceAsk.basis: The market verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'. Our ₹67.47 L annual spend gives us the volume to reach that lower band. The open-market shows caps quoted from ₹0.55 up to ₹1.20/pc — there is room to move down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep current 30-day terms; no push for earlier payment at this stage.

brief.financialLeverage: Empire publishes no financials, so we can't see inside their books. That means we build our case purely on what the market charges and on having other options lined up. We spend ₹67.47 L a year with them — a mid-sized account that matters, but not so big we can squeeze hard without alternatives. The smart play is to show them we're shopping around (Manjushree, Mold-Tek, and others are real second sources) and that the market price band supports a cut to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at our volume. Push firmly but don't corner them — we need visibility into their cost structure first.

evidence.point: Our annual spend with Empire is ₹67.47 L
The market asking range for a 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, with typical quotes ₹0.85–0.95/pc
The market verdict states there is modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec
HDPE resin import unit value stands at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material reference point
We currently pay on 30 Days After Receipt terms

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Revenue of ₹2569.83 Cr and health score B (65/100). Top second-source candidate — a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ).

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader covering pails, containers, and pharma packaging. Strong and profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures — a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ).

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed company with moulded and blow-moulded packaging capability across bottles and caps — a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ).

risks: Empire's financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on their cost base and how much margin they carry — verify their maker vs. trader role before pushing too hard.
The market ask shows 'MARKET-FAIR' — our current price may already be reasonable; if we push below ₹0.65/pc without volume commitment, we risk a 'no' or a quality cut.

We have no internal best-price benchmark (no other vendor for this exact item), so our ask rests entirely on the market band and alternates — line up at least one firm RFQ from Manjushree or Mold-Tek before the meeting to prove the price is real.
Switching to an alternate will take 2–3 months for tooling and qualification — don't threaten to walk unless we're ready to actually move the business.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're reviewing all our rigid-plastic packaging spend, and the market is quoting 28 mm caps at ₹0.55–1.20, with a typical band of ₹0.85–0.95 — at our ₹67.47 L annual volume, we'd like to discuss moving our price down toward ₹0.65–0.80.
